2608.30980.title: Evaluating and Improving LLM Self-Modeling
2608.30980.paper_summary: We study self-modeling: an LLM's ability to answer questions about its own behavior. We focus on verifiable behavioral questions, such as whether a prompt edit would change the model's final answer. To measure this capability, we introduce a benchmark that tests diverse types of self-modeling questions. Current models show non-trivial but limited self-modeling skill, and make systematic mistakes on simple counterfactual questions about their own behavior. To improve self-modeling skill, we develop a scalable synthetic-data pipeline that produces self-modeling training data, and show that reinforcement-learning can improve aggregate self-modeling skill across three open-source model families with some transfer to held-out tasks. These gains, however, do not seem to constitute introspection consistently: improved self-modeling may not arise from privileged access to the model's internal decision process.
2608.30980.paper_summary_zh: 我們研究自我建模：大型語言模型（LLM）回答有關其自身行為問題的能力。<lb/>我們專注於可驗證的行為問題，例如提示編輯是否會改變模型的最終答案。<lb/>為了測量這一能力，我們引入了一個基準，測試各種自我建模問題。<lb/>目前的模型顯示出非平凡但有限的自我建模技能，並在關於其自身行為的簡單反事實問題上犯系統性錯誤。<lb/>為了提高自我建模技能，我們開發了一個可擴展的合成數據管道，生成自我建模訓練數據，並顯示增強學習可以提高三個開源模型系列的整體自我建模技能，並在某些保留任務中有一定的轉移。<lb/>然而，這些增益似乎並不總是構成內省：改進的自我建模可能並非源於對模型內部決策過程的特權訪問。
